questions.q: 生命如何、在哪里、为何起源？
questions.q_en: How, where, and why did life originate?

questions.q: 什么是生命，它有没有一个统一的定义？
questions.q_en: What is life, and is there a unified definition of it?

questions.q: 我们在宇宙中孤独吗？
questions.q_en: Are we alone in the universe?

questions.q: 衰老与死亡是必然的吗？
questions.q_en: Are aging and death inevitable?

questions.q: 意识为何、如何从物质中产生（意识的「硬问题」）？
questions.q_en: Why and how does consciousness arise from matter (the hard problem)?

questions.q: 智能与智慧如何从物质中诞生，它们的演化是否遵循可被重复发现的规律？
questions.q_en: How do intelligence and wisdom arise from matter — and does their evolution follow laws we could rediscover?

questions.q: 几十年的记忆如何被储存进一团脑组织，又如何在一瞬间被精准提取？
questions.q_en: How is a lifetime of memory stored in a lump of brain tissue — and retrieved, precisely, in an instant?

questions.q: 自由意志存在吗？
questions.q_en: Does free will exist?

questions.q: 暗物质究竟是什么——是一种看不见的新粒子，还是我们把引力定律写错了？
questions.q_en: What is dark matter — an unseen new kind of particle, or a sign we have written the law of gravity wrong?

questions.q: 暗能量是什么，宇宙最终将如何终结？
questions.q_en: What is dark energy, and how will the universe end?

questions.q: 时间、空间与物质本身从何而来，一个「开端」如何可能凭空出现？
questions.q_en: Where do time, space, and matter themselves come from — and how can a "beginning" arise at all?

questions.q: 时间是什么，它为何只朝一个方向流动？
questions.q_en: What is time, and why does it have a direction?

questions.q: 描述微观的量子论与描述时空的引力论各自精准却互相矛盾，它们能被缝成一套理论吗？
questions.q_en: Quantum theory (the very small) and gravity (spacetime) are each precise yet mutually contradictory — can they be sewn into one theory?

questions.q: 自然有没有一个最终的、统一的理论？
questions.q_en: Is there a final, unified theory of nature?

questions.q: 物理常数为何恰好如此，使宇宙能容纳生命（精细调节）？
questions.q_en: Why are the physical constants fine-tuned so the universe can host life?

questions.q: 数学为何能如此「不合理地」有效地描述自然？
questions.q_en: Why is mathematics so unreasonably effective at describing nature?

questions.q: 计算有没有根本极限（P 是否等于 NP）？
questions.q_en: Are there fundamental limits to computation (does P = NP)?

questions.q: 在人人自利的世界里，合作为何能演化出来？
questions.q_en: Why does cooperation evolve in a world of self-interest?

questions.q: 人与机器将如何共同演化？
questions.q_en: How will humans and machines co-evolve?

questions.q: 有没有一些真理，因逻辑、宇宙视界或计算代价而被永远挡在认知之外？
questions.q_en: Are there truths permanently beyond reach — barred by logic, by the cosmic horizon, or by computational cost?

questions.q: 文明能否预测并避免自身的崩溃？
questions.q_en: Can a civilization predict and avoid its own collapse?

questions.q: 我们如何发现「未知的未知」？
questions.q_en: How do we discover the unknown unknowns?

questions.q: 信息是不是比物质更基础（万物源于比特）？
questions.q_en: Is information more fundamental than matter (it from bit)?

questions.q: 科学发现能被自动化到什么程度，人类不可替代的内核是什么？
questions.q_en: How far can scientific discovery be automated, and what is the irreplaceable human core?

questions.q: 地球气候系统藏着多少不可逆的临界点，跨过去之后还能回头吗？
questions.q_en: How many irreversible tipping points hide in Earth's climate, and can we turn back after crossing one?

questions.q: 一串 DNA 字母如何被「读」成一个完整的身体，从基因型到表型的映射有没有可破译的规律？
questions.q_en: How is a string of DNA letters read into a whole body, and is the genotype-to-phenotype map decipherable?

questions.q: 信息有没有物理实体，擦除一个比特为何必须付出热的代价？
questions.q_en: Is information physical, and why must erasing a single bit cost heat?

questions.q: 为什么「多」会变得「不同」，全新的规律如何从简单部件的堆叠中涌现？
questions.q_en: Why is more different, and how do brand-new laws emerge from simply stacking simple parts?

questions.q: 湍流——经典物理最古老的未解之谜——能否被真正理解和预测？
questions.q_en: Turbulence, the oldest unsolved problem of classical physics, can it ever be understood and predicted?

questions.q: 为什么宇宙里有物质而几乎没有反物质，我们存在本身从何而来？
questions.q_en: Why is the universe made of matter and almost no antimatter, and where does our very existence come from?

questions.q: 演化为何会一次次跨越「重大转变」，从单细胞走向多细胞、从个体走向社会，复杂性是必然还是侥幸？
questions.q_en: Why does evolution keep crossing major transitions, from single cells to bodies to societies, and is rising complexity inevitable or a fluke?

questions.q: 经济有没有可被发现的「定律」，繁荣、泡沫与崩盘究竟能不能被预测？
questions.q_en: Does the economy obey discoverable laws, and can booms, bubbles, and crashes actually be predicted?

questions.q: 为什么存在「有」，而不是一无所有？
questions.q_en: Why is there something rather than nothing?

questions.q: 黑洞蒸发时，掉进去的信息是被永久抹去，还是悄悄逃了出来（黑洞信息悖论）？
questions.q_en: When a black hole evaporates, is the information that fell in destroyed forever, or does it secretly escape (the black-hole information paradox)?

questions.q: 大爆炸之前有没有「之前」，暴胀真的发生过吗？
questions.q_en: Was there a before the Big Bang, and did cosmic inflation really happen?

questions.q: 宇宙是有限的还是无限的，它的整体形状是什么？
questions.q_en: Is the universe finite or infinite, and what is its overall shape?

questions.q: 遗传密码从何而来，把三联码翻译成氨基酸的这套规则是必然、冻结的偶然，还是被优化出来的？
questions.q_en: Where did the genetic code come from, and is the rule that maps triplets to amino acids a necessity, a frozen accident, or an optimized choice?

questions.q: 一颗受精卵如何知道该在哪里长出眼睛、心脏和手指，把自己折叠成一个有形的身体（形态发生）？
questions.q_en: How does a single fertilized egg know where to grow eyes, a heart, and fingers, folding itself into a shaped body (morphogenesis)?

questions.q: 既然有性繁殖代价高昂、还要花一半资源生出不能生育的雄性，它为何能演化出来并主宰了生命世界？
questions.q_en: Given that sex is costly and wastes half the effort on males who bear no young, why did it evolve and come to dominate life?

questions.q: 是什么触发了地球历史上的大灭绝，我们正在制造的「第六次大灭绝」会走到哪一步？
questions.q_en: What triggers Earth's mass extinctions, and how far will the sixth one we are now causing go?

questions.q: 地震到底能不能被预测，还是说它在原理上就不可预报？
questions.q_en: Can earthquakes be predicted at all, or are they unpredictable in principle?

questions.q: 数学是被人类发明的，还是本就存在、等着被发现？
questions.q_en: Is mathematics invented by humans, or does it exist independently, waiting to be discovered?

questions.q: 黎曼猜想成立吗——素数的分布是否真的隐藏着一条完美的秩序？
questions.q_en: Is the Riemann hypothesis true — do the primes really hide a perfect underlying order?

questions.q: 哥德尔与图灵的不可判定性会不会给物理学本身划下根本极限，让有些物理问题原则上就无法计算？
questions.q_en: Do the undecidability results of Goedel and Turing set fundamental limits on physics itself, making some physical questions uncomputable in principle?

questions.q: 我们为什么要睡觉——把人生三分之一交给一种危险又无防备的状态，到底换来了什么？
questions.q_en: Why do we sleep — what do we gain by surrendering a third of life to a dangerous, defenseless state?

questions.q: 语言从何而来——是什么让人类独有了能从有限词汇生成无限句子的能力？
questions.q_en: Where did language come from — what gave humans alone the power to generate infinite sentences from finite words?

questions.q: 量子的「测量问题」如何解决——一旦我们去看,叠加的可能性为何瞬间塌缩成唯一的现实？
questions.q_en: How is the quantum measurement problem solved — why, the moment we look, does a superposition of possibilities collapse into a single reality?

questions.q: 高温超导的机制到底是什么——为什么某些材料能在远高于预期的温度下让电流毫无阻力地流动？
questions.q_en: What is the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity — why do some materials carry current with zero resistance far above the temperatures theory expects?

questions.q: 蛋白质如何在一瞬间从一维序列自动折叠成精确的三维形状,这套「折叠密码」能被破译吗？
questions.q_en: How does a protein fold from a one-dimensional sequence into its exact three-dimensional shape in an instant, and can this folding code be cracked?

questions.q: 是什么维系着生物多样性——为什么成百上千个物种能在有限的资源里长期共存而不互相淘汰？
questions.q_en: What sustains biodiversity — why can hundreds of competing species coexist on limited resources for the long run instead of driving each other extinct?

questions.q: 我们能否设计并「写」出一整套基因组，让一个选定的生物按我们的意图运行？
questions.q_en: Can we design and write a whole genome that programs a chosen organism to our intent?

questions.q: 物质能否跨越所有尺度变得完全可编程，像写软件一样写出它的形状与性能？
questions.q_en: Can matter be made fully programmable across scales, so its shape and properties are written like software?

questions.q: 有没有一套理论，能解释学习系统——无论是大脑还是机器——何时以及为何能举一反三？
questions.q_en: Is there a theory that explains when and why learning systems, brains and machines alike, generalize?

questions.q: 我们能否预测并引导大规模社会系统，却不因此抹杀个体的自主性？
questions.q_en: Can large-scale social systems be predicted and steered without eliminating individual agency?

questions.q: 我们能否在与我们截然不同的系统里，测量出意识或主观体验是否存在？
questions.q_en: Can we measure whether consciousness or experience exists in systems unlike us?

collisions.shared: 两者都在问：一堆局部过程在什么条件下融成一个整体——主观体验的统一，与从特例到通则的泛化。
collisions.shared_en: Both ask when a swarm of local processes fuses into one whole — the unity of experience vs generalizing from instances to a rule.
collisions.synthesis: 第一人称的「体验统一」与机器的「举一反三」，是否依赖同一种「信息整合」越过某个阈值？
collisions.synthesis_en: Do the unity of first-person experience and a machine’s leap from examples to a rule both hinge on integrated information crossing one threshold?

collisions.shared: 一边是客观世界为何能被抽象符号精准描述，一边是主观体验为何能从客观物质里冒出——都横跨主客之裂。
collisions.shared_en: One side: why the objective world yields to abstract symbols. The other: why subjective experience arises from objective matter. Both straddle the subject–object rift.
collisions.synthesis: 宇宙既能被数学完全描述、又能从内部「被体验」，这两件「过于巧合」的事，会不会指向同一个未知前提？
collisions.synthesis_en: The universe is exactly describable by math, and is also experienced from inside — could these two “too lucky” facts point to one unknown premise?

collisions.shared: 不可判定性说「有些结局原则上算不出」，自由意志问「未来是否被前因定死」——都关乎未来是否已被封进现在。
collisions.shared_en: Undecidability says some outcomes can’t be computed in principle; free will asks whether the future is fixed by the past — both about whether the future is already sealed in the present.
collisions.synthesis: 若有些事在原理上不可计算，未来对宇宙自身也是「未写定」的——这是否给自由意志留了一道逻辑的缝？
collisions.synthesis_en: If some outcomes are uncomputable even in principle, the future is unwritten even to the universe — does that leave a logical gap for free will?

collisions.shared: 找蛋白质的最低能量构象是已知的 NP 难问题，可它毫秒折好——自然像是在「免费」解一道难题。
collisions.shared_en: Finding a protein’s minimum-energy fold is NP-hard, yet it happens in milliseconds — nature seems to solve a hard problem “for free.”
collisions.synthesis: 蛋白质毫秒折叠、晶体退火、量子系统寻基态——自然是不是在物理上「绕过」了我们以为不可高效求解的难题？
collisions.synthesis_en: Proteins fold in milliseconds, crystals anneal, quantum systems find ground states — is nature physically “bypassing” problems we deem intractable?

collisions.shared: 都是「只能通过它做了什么、而非它是什么来认出它」——暗物质靠引力足迹，生命靠它的行为。
collisions.shared_en: Both are known only by what they do, not what they are — dark matter by its gravitational footprint, life by its behavior.
collisions.synthesis: 如果暗物质与生命都只能「凭效果」而非「凭定义」来辨认，那「凭效果定义存在」本身是不是一种更深的科学方法？
collisions.synthesis_en: If we identify both dark matter and life only by effect, not definition, is “defining existence by its effects” itself a deeper method?

collisions.shared: 两者都是跨尺度、强耦合、拒绝被还原成零件的涌现现象。
collisions.shared_en: Both are cross-scale, strongly-coupled emergent phenomena that refuse reduction to their parts.
collisions.synthesis: 意识会不会是一种「神经湍流」——一种跨尺度、自相似、无法从单个神经元推出的动力学相？
collisions.synthesis_en: Could consciousness be a kind of “neural turbulence” — a cross-scale, self-similar dynamical phase no single neuron implies?

collisions.shared: 量子测量问「叠加为何塌缩成唯一现实」，自由意志问「一个确定的脑如何做出真正的选择」——都在追问「确定 vs 开放」（注：二者的关联本身有争议）。
collisions.shared_en: Measurement asks why superposition collapses to one reality; free will asks how a determinate brain truly chooses — both probe “determinate vs open” (their link is itself contested).
collisions.synthesis: 量子的不确定与「选择」之间，究竟是真有因果联系，还是我们把两种不同的「开放性」混为一谈了？
collisions.synthesis_en: Between quantum indeterminacy and “choice,” is there a real causal link — or are we conflating two different kinds of openness?

collisions.shared: 若实在以信息为本，黑洞「能否抹掉信息」就成了「实在能否被删除」的终极测试。
collisions.shared_en: If reality is information at bottom, whether a black hole can erase information becomes the ultimate test of whether reality can be deleted.
collisions.synthesis: 黑洞信息悖论是否其实是「万物源于比特」的判决性实验——宇宙到底允不允许信息被彻底抹去？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is the black-hole information paradox the decisive test of “it from bit” — does the universe permit information to be truly erased?

collisions.shared: 都是高维、强反馈、跨尺度的混沌系统，精确预测在原理上就极难。
collisions.shared_en: Both are high-dimensional, strongly-feedback, cross-scale chaotic systems where precise prediction is hard in principle.
collisions.synthesis: 金融崩盘与湍流是否服从同一类「临界级联」数学——若是，经济的不可预测就不是缺数据，而是本质？
collisions.synthesis_en: Do market crashes and turbulence obey the same critical-cascade math — if so, the economy’s unpredictability is fundamental, not a data gap?

collisions.shared: 遗传密码是「冻结的偶然」却出奇地抗错最优；数学是「凭空发明」却出奇地有效——两个「不该这么好」的映射。
collisions.shared_en: The genetic code is a “frozen accident” yet near-optimally error-robust; math is “invented” yet uncannily effective — two mappings that are “too good.”
collisions.synthesis: 遗传密码的近乎最优，与数学的「不合理有效」，会不会都是「被选择/被筛出的映射」这同一回事？
collisions.synthesis_en: The genetic code’s near-optimality and math’s “unreasonable effectiveness” — are both just “a mapping that got selected/filtered”?

collisions.shared: 重大转变需要部件「为整体牺牲」；程序性死亡正是细胞为身体让位——死亡或是合作的工具。
collisions.shared_en: Major transitions need parts to sacrifice for the whole; programmed death is cells yielding for the body — death may be a tool of cooperation.
collisions.synthesis: 个体的衰老与死亡，是不是「更高层级的我」得以稳定存在所必须付出的代价？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are ageing and death the price a higher-level “self” must pay to exist stably?

collisions.shared: 睡眠重整突触、巩固记忆——它维护的，正是记忆所搭建的那个「自我」。
collisions.shared_en: Sleep renormalizes synapses and consolidates memory — what it maintains is the very “self” that memory builds.
collisions.synthesis: 如果睡眠的核心功能是维护记忆与突触，那「自我在时间中的连续」是不是每晚都要被重写一次才能续命？
collisions.synthesis_en: If sleep’s core job is maintaining memory and synapses, must the self’s continuity be rewritten nightly to persist?

collisions.shared: 「何时算活着」与「何时有体验」都是同一类边界问题——一个系统从何时起拥有了「内部」。
collisions.shared_en: “When does it count as alive” and “when does it experience” are the same boundary problem — when a system comes to have an inside.
collisions.synthesis: 「是不是活的」与「有没有体验」，是两个独立的门槛，还是「拥有一个内部视角」这同一道门槛的两面？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are “is it alive” and “does it experience” two thresholds, or two faces of one — having an inside?

collisions.shared: 宇宙学常数是物理学最严重的精细调节问题——暗能量的数值小得离谱却又非零。
collisions.shared_en: The cosmological constant is physics’ worst fine-tuning problem — dark energy’s value is absurdly small yet nonzero.
collisions.synthesis: 暗能量为何小得离谱却不为零——这道精细调节难题，是多重宇宙人择的最强证据，还是它最大的尴尬？
collisions.synthesis_en: Why is dark energy absurdly tiny yet nonzero — is this fine-tuning the strongest case for the anthropic multiverse, or its biggest embarrassment?

collisions.shared: 「不可预测」可能不是「随机」，而是「计算上不可行」——两种截然不同的不可知。
collisions.shared_en: “Unpredictable” may mean not “random” but “computationally infeasible” — two very different kinds of unknowable.
collisions.synthesis: 经济危机的「不可预测」，究竟是真随机，还是只是一道我们算不动的 NP 难题？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is a financial crisis’s unpredictability true randomness, or just an NP-hard problem we can’t compute?

collisions.shared: 「时空从纠缠中涌现」纲领把引力几何变成了信息几何。
collisions.shared_en: The “spacetime from entanglement” program turns the geometry of gravity into the geometry of information.
collisions.synthesis: 如果时空是由量子纠缠编织出来的，那引力是不是根本就是「信息的几何」？
collisions.synthesis_en: If spacetime is woven from entanglement, is gravity simply the geometry of information?

collisions.shared: 气候临界点就是相变——同一套临界现象、序参量与早期预警的数学。
collisions.shared_en: A climate tipping point is a phase transition — the same math of critical phenomena, order parameters, and early-warning signals.
collisions.synthesis: 地球的临界点、磁体的相变、文明的崩溃，是不是同一门「临界涌现」科学的不同实例？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are Earth’s tipping points, a magnet’s phase transition, and a civilization’s collapse instances of one “critical emergence” science?

collisions.shared: 素数的隐秘秩序疑似对应某个量子系统的能级——纯数学竟与物理同构。
collisions.shared_en: The primes’ hidden order may correspond to a quantum system’s energy levels — pure mathematics turning out isomorphic to physics.
collisions.synthesis: 若黎曼零点真是某个物理系统的能级，那「数学描述自然」是否要反过来说——自然里本就藏着数论？
collisions.synthesis_en: If Riemann’s zeros are a physical system’s energy levels, should “math describes nature” be reversed — is number theory already hiding in nature?

collisions.shared: 当机器开始定义什么叫智能，「人类智能是否还是参照系」本身成了变量。
collisions.shared_en: Once machines begin to define intelligence, whether human intelligence is still the reference frame becomes a variable itself.
collisions.synthesis: 当机器智能反过来重塑我们对「智能」的定义，我们还能用人类作为衡量智能的基准吗？
collisions.synthesis_en: As machine intelligence reshapes what “intelligence” means, can we still use humans as the yardstick?

collisions.shared: 自动化发现能高速搜索已知问题空间，却最难处理「我们没想到要问的问题」。
collisions.shared_en: Automated discovery can search the known problem space fast, but struggles most with the questions we never thought to ask.
collisions.synthesis: 一台能自动做科学的机器，能不能发现「未知的未知」——还是说照亮盲区恰恰是人不可替代的内核？
collisions.synthesis_en: Can a machine that automates science find the unknown unknowns — or is lighting up blind spots the irreplaceable human core?

collisions.shared: 都在问「自利的个体如何汇成可持续、可被引导的集体」——从演化到舆论。
collisions.shared_en: Both ask how self-interested individuals assemble into a sustainable, steerable collective — from evolution to public opinion.
collisions.synthesis: 让细胞甘愿合作的那套规则，能不能用来设计「既稳健协作、又不抹杀个体自主」的人类社会？
collisions.synthesis_en: Can the rules that make cells cooperate be used to design a human society that’s both robustly cooperative and free?

collisions.shared: 记忆只指向过去、时间只流向未来——这两个「方向」可能同源于熵增。
collisions.shared_en: Memory points only to the past; time flows only forward — both “directions” may share one root in rising entropy.
collisions.synthesis: 我们之所以记得过去而非未来，与时间只朝一个方向流，是不是同一道「熵之箭」的两个侧面？
collisions.synthesis_en: Do we remember the past (not the future), and does time flow one way, because of one and the same arrow of entropy?

collisions.shared: 一边说信息必有物理代价（兰道尔），一边说物理源于信息（惠勒）——信息与物质谁更基础正面相撞。
collisions.shared_en: One side: information must pay a physical cost (Landauer). The other: physics arises from information (Wheeler). Which is more fundamental collides head-on.
collisions.synthesis: 信息到底是「必须付热的物理量」，还是「物理由之而生的本原」——这两种看法能否在同一套理论里和解？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is information a physical quantity that must pay heat, or the origin physics springs from — can the two views be reconciled in one theory?

collisions.shared: 都是「一个微小、早期、被冻结的不对称，决定了后来的一切」。
collisions.shared_en: Both are “one tiny early asymmetry, frozen in, that determined everything after.”
collisions.synthesis: 宇宙的物质盈余与生命的手性/密码，是不是同一类「早期微小不对称被永久放大」的故事？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are the cosmos’s matter surplus and life’s chirality/code the same story — a tiny early asymmetry frozen and amplified forever?

collisions.shared: 一团均匀细胞自发长出精确图案，正是「多即不同」的活体案例——涌现出零件里没有的形态。
collisions.shared_en: A uniform ball of cells spontaneously forming precise pattern is “more is different” alive — a form no part contains.
collisions.synthesis: 胚胎自组织出身体，与磁体自发磁化，是不是同一门「自发图案涌现」的科学？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is an embryo self-organizing a body the same “spontaneous pattern emergence” science as a magnet magnetizing itself?

collisions.shared: 一个问「为何只有我们」，一个问「为何有任何东西」——都把「我们的存在」当成需要解释的反常。
collisions.shared_en: One asks “why only us,” the other “why anything at all” — both treat our existence as an anomaly demanding explanation.
collisions.synthesis: 「我们为何在这」与「为何有『有』」，会不会最终都得诉诸同一种人择式的「幸存者偏差」？
collisions.synthesis_en: Do “why are we here” and “why is there anything” both ultimately appeal to the same anthropic survivor’s bias?

collisions.shared: 一个追求「万物的终极方程」，一个怀疑「有些真理原则上够不着」——终极理论会不会撞上认知天花板。
collisions.shared_en: One seeks the ultimate equation; the other suspects some truths are unreachable in principle — could the final theory hit the ceiling of the knowable.
collisions.synthesis: 万物之理若存在，它会不会恰恰是那种「存在却永远证不出/算不出」的真理？
collisions.synthesis_en: If a theory of everything exists, might it be exactly the kind of truth that exists yet can never be proven or computed?

collisions.shared: 高温超导是「多即不同」最棘手的样本——大量强关联电子涌现出谁也算不准的新相。
collisions.shared_en: High-Tc is the hardest case of “more is different” — many strongly-correlated electrons emerging into a phase no one can compute.
collisions.synthesis: 破解高温超导，是不是要先有一门能预言「强关联涌现」的通用涌现理论，而非只补一个机制？
collisions.synthesis_en: Does cracking high-Tc require a general theory of strongly-correlated emergence first, rather than patching in one mechanism?

collisions.shared: 「我们能否制造生命」是「什么是生命」的工程版判决——做得出来，才算真懂。
collisions.shared_en: “Can we make life” is the engineering verdict on “what is life” — to build it is to truly understand it.
collisions.synthesis: 如果我们能从零写出一套会自我维持、会演化的基因组，那是不是就用「造得出」回答了「什么是生命」？
collisions.synthesis_en: If we can write a self-sustaining, evolving genome from scratch, do we answer “what is life” by building it?

collisions.shared: 个体层面争论「选择是否自由」，群体层面却发现行为高度可预测、可被算法推动——自由与可预测的张力。
collisions.shared_en: At the individual level we debate whether choice is free; at the aggregate level behavior is highly predictable and algorithm-nudgeable — the tension of freedom vs predictability.
collisions.synthesis: 如果亿万个「自由」选择在总体上高度可预测、可被操纵，那个体自由意志与社会可预测性如何并存？
collisions.synthesis_en: If billions of “free” choices are highly predictable and nudge-able in aggregate, how do individual free will and social predictability coexist?

collisions.shared: 都是「一个全新层级如何从一个没有它的状态里第一次出现」——宇宙从无到有，生命从非生到生。
collisions.shared_en: Both are “how a brand-new level first appears from a state without it” — cosmos from nothing, life from non-life.
collisions.synthesis: 宇宙的诞生与生命的起源，是不是同一类「第一次出现」问题——一个全新层级如何从不含它的状态里跃出？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are the birth of the universe and the origin of life the same kind of “first appearance” — how a wholly new level leaps from a state that lacks it?

collisions.shared: 重大转变是「更高层级如何建立」，崩溃是「它如何瓦解」——同一座复杂度阶梯的上行与下行。
collisions.shared_en: Major transitions are “how a higher level is built”; collapse is “how it comes apart” — the climb and the fall of one ladder of complexity.
collisions.synthesis: 复杂度的攀升（重大转变）与崩塌（文明崩溃），是不是同一座阶梯的上行与下行，受同一组力支配？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are the rise of complexity (major transitions) and its collapse (civilizational breakdown) the up and down of one staircase, governed by one set of forces?

collisions.shared: 从 DNA 序列预测表型，和从数据学到能泛化的函数，都是「从一维代码推出高维行为」的映射难题。
collisions.shared_en: Predicting phenotype from DNA and learning a function that generalizes are both the hard problem of inferring high-dimensional behavior from a one-dimensional code.
collisions.synthesis: 「从基因型预测表型」与「机器学习的泛化」，是不是同一个「从一维代码推出高维行为」的映射问题，可共享一套理论？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are “predicting phenotype from genotype” and “generalization in machine learning” the same mapping problem — inferring high-dimensional behavior from a 1-D code — sharing one theory?

collisions.shared: 一个问「时间有没有起点之前」，一个问「空间有没有边界之外」——都在追问观测视界之外的整体结构。
collisions.shared_en: One asks whether there is a “before” the beginning, the other whether there is a “beyond” the edge — both probe the whole structure past the observational horizon.
collisions.synthesis: 时间的「之前」与空间的「之外」，是不是同一道「可观测宇宙之外还有什么」问题的两面？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are time’s “before” and space’s “beyond” two faces of one question — what lies outside the observable universe?

collisions.shared: 有性繁殖维持基因多样性，物种共存维持生态多样性——都在问「多样性为何能对抗『单一最优者通吃』」。
collisions.shared_en: Sex maintains genetic diversity; coexistence maintains ecological diversity — both ask why diversity withstands “the single optimum taking all.”
collisions.synthesis: 维持基因多样性的性，与维持物种多样性的共存机制，是不是同一种「多样性如何抵御赢家通吃」的策略？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are sex (which maintains genetic diversity) and coexistence mechanisms (which maintain species diversity) the same strategy — how diversity resists winner-take-all?

collisions.shared: 大灭绝清空生态位，往往紧跟着演化的爆发与重大转变——毁灭与创造在生命史上交替。
collisions.shared_en: Mass extinctions empty niches and are often followed by evolutionary bursts and major transitions — destruction and creation alternate across the history of life.
collisions.synthesis: 大灭绝是否是演化创新的「重置键」——毁灭与重大转变的爆发，是不是同一台引擎的两个冲程？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is mass extinction the “reset button” of evolutionary innovation — are destruction and the burst of major transitions two strokes of one engine?

collisions.shared: 地震与金融崩盘都疑似自组织临界——微小扰动以幂律分布级联放大，何时引爆原则上不可预报。
collisions.shared_en: Earthquakes and crashes both look self-organized-critical — small perturbations cascade with power-law statistics, and when they detonate is unforecastable in principle.
collisions.synthesis: 地震与股灾，是不是同一类「自组织临界」系统——大事件的不可预报，是本质而非数据不足？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are earthquakes and market crashes the same “self-organized criticality” system — is the unforecastability of large events fundamental, not a data shortage?

collisions.shared: 黎曼猜想若描述的是素数里早已存在的隐秘秩序，那它支持「数学是被发现的」而非被发明的。
collisions.shared_en: If the Riemann Hypothesis describes an order already present among the primes, it favors mathematics being discovered rather than invented.
collisions.synthesis: 素数里那条「等待被发现」的隐秘秩序，是不是「数学是发现而非发明」的最有力证据？
collisions.synthesis_en: Is the hidden order “waiting to be found” among the primes the strongest evidence that mathematics is discovered, not invented?

collisions.shared: 哥德尔不完备已渗入物理（谱隙不可判定），意味着「万物之理」里可能藏着原则上算不出的物理问题。
collisions.shared_en: Gödelian incompleteness already seeps into physics (the undecidable spectral gap), so a theory of everything may harbor physical questions uncomputable in principle.
collisions.synthesis: 如果不可判定性能渗入物理定律，那一套「万物之理」里会不会必然包含它自己永远算不出的预测？
collisions.synthesis_en: If undecidability can seep into physical law, must a “theory of everything” necessarily contain predictions it can never compute about itself?

collisions.shared: 大语言模型从零「学会」无限句法，给「人类语言如何起源」提供了第一个非人类的对照实验。
collisions.shared_en: Large language models learning unbounded syntax from scratch offer the first non-human control experiment for how human language arose.
collisions.synthesis: 机器从数据中习得语言，能否反过来揭示人类语言的起源——还是说它走的是一条完全不同的路？
collisions.synthesis_en: Can machines learning language from data illuminate the origin of human language — or do they take an entirely different route?

collisions.shared: 「把物质编程」与「编写基因组」都是把工程变成「书写」——让材料/生命像软件一样按指令运行。
collisions.shared_en: “Programming matter” and “writing a genome” both turn engineering into writing — making material or life run by instruction, like software.
collisions.synthesis: 「给物质编程」和「编写生命」，是不是同一场「让物质照着我们写的代码运行」的工程革命的两条战线？
collisions.synthesis_en: Are “programming matter” and “writing life” two fronts of one engineering revolution — making matter run the code we write?

collisions.shared: 当机器越来越像有心智，「能否从外部测出体验」直接决定我们对 AI 负有什么道德义务。
collisions.shared_en: As machines grow more mind-like, whether experience can be measured from outside directly decides what moral duties we owe to AI.
collisions.synthesis: 如果我们造出行为上酷似有意识的机器，却无法测出它是否真有体验，该如何决定对它的道德义务？
collisions.synthesis_en: If we build machines that behave as if conscious, yet can’t measure whether they truly experience, how do we decide our moral obligations to them?
